title: Bitset optimization tricks
relevance: Medium — rarely named “bitset” in OAs, but the *packed boolean / subset-sum reachability* idea (Partition Equal Subset Sum, “can you make sum S?”) shows up constantly; dense AND/OR / DAG reachability is a Candidate Master rating-builder Striver never covers.
company_notes: Partition Equal Subset Sum / subset with sum S — bool knapsack; bitset is the CP-speed version. Team sizes after merging friend groups — DSU component sizes + subset-sum (School Excursion). n≤2000 bitstrings/rows counting pairs on columns — packed AND/XOR + popcount (Corner Subgrid / Oddly Similar). Can u reach v in a large digraph / many queries — SCC + bitset reachability (CSES Reachability Queries), not Floyd on n=1e5.

phases.goal: Spot when boolean reachability/adjacency at large dimension calls for packed bitset ops rather than plain bool arrays or bitmask DP.

must_hit.point: When DP/state is boolean (reachable / adjacent / exists) and the dimension is thousands, pack bits into machine words (std::bitset / uint64_t[]) so AND/OR/XOR/shift run ~64× faster.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names boolean state at large dimension and packed words for word-parallel AND/OR/XOR/shift.

must_hit.point: Classic tells: subset-sum with n·W too big but n·W/64 OK → dp |= dp << w; pairwise row/column overlaps → AND then .count(); DAG/SCC reachability → OR bitsets along topo; complement-graph BFS → _Find_next over an unvisited bitset.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists at least two of: knapsack shift, pairwise AND+count, topo OR, complement _Find_next.

must_hit.point: Recognize constraints like n≤2e3–5e3 with an n² or n·W bool loop that needs a /64 constant.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites n≤2e3–5e3-scale n² or n·W bool work and the /64 speedup cue.

probes: When do you reach for bitset packing instead of a plain bool array or bitmask DP?
What constraint shapes scream n·W/64 or n²/64 rather than naive boolean DP?

hints.1: Ask whether the state is only reachable/exists and the dimension is in the thousands.
hints.2: Map the ask to subset-sum shift, pairwise AND+count, topo OR, or complement _Find_next.
hints.3: Say: boolean state at large dimension → pack into words (~64×); tells are dp |= dp << w, (A&B).count(), topo OR, unvisited _Find_next; watch n≤2e3–5e3 with n² or n·W needing /64.

phases.goal: State the core bitset templates: knapsack shift, pairwise AND/XOR, DAG/SCC OR, and complement traversal.

must_hit.point: Subset-sum reachability: dp[0]=1; for w in a: dp |= dp << w (0/1); for bounded counts, binary-split multiplicities then shift.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the shift-OR 0/1 update and mentions binary-split for bounded multiplicities.

must_hit.point: Pairwise overlap: store each row/set as a bitset; answer = (A & B).count() (or XOR for parity-of-matches).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Stores rows/sets as bitsets and uses AND+count or XOR for parity.

must_hit.point: DAG reachability: reach[u][u]=1; for u in topo: for v in adj[u]: reach[u] |= reach[v] (direction depends on edge meaning); SCC queries: Kosaraju/Tarjan → DAG on components → same bitset OR on the condensation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes topo OR of reach bitsets and SCC condensation before the same trick.

must_hit.point: Complement-graph traversal: keep unvisited vertices in a bitset/set; iterate with _Find_first / _Find_next, skip real neighbors.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps an unvisited bitset and walks with _Find_first/_Find_next while skipping adj neighbors.

probes: How do you encode 0/1 subset-sum reachability with a bitset?
How do DAG reachability and complement-graph BFS use bitsets differently?

hints.1: One template shifts a reachability bitset; another ORs along a topo order.
hints.2: 0/1: dp |= dp << w; pairs: (A&B).count(); DAG: OR children’s reach on topo; complement: _Find_next on unvisited.
hints.3: State dp[0]=1 then dp |= dp << w (binary-split if bounded counts); pairs AND/XOR+count; reach[u]|=reach[v] on topo after setting reach[u][u]; SCC first then same OR; unvisited bitset with _Find_first/_Find_next skipping real neighbors.

phases.goal: Show how to write the bitset ops and the standard shift / AND / topo-OR / _Find_next loops.

must_hit.point: bitset<N> ops (AND/OR/XOR/shift/.count()/.test()/.set()) cost O(N/64); prefer compile-time N or your own uint64_t blocks when N is dynamic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the ops and prefers fixed N or manual uint64_t blocks for dynamic length.

must_hit.point: Money Sums / partition style: mark reachable sums with dp |= dp << w; Partition Equal Subset Sum family is the same bool knapsack with bitset speedup.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes or narrates the shift-OR knapsack and ties it to equal-sum / sum-S checks.

must_hit.point: Corner Subgrid Count shape: pair-rows AND + C(k,2) — the O(n²·n/64) bitset AND classic (n≤3000); Oddly Similar uses column-value XOR bitsets for odd #matches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes row-pair AND then popcount (and C(k,2) or XOR-parity variant).

must_hit.point: 0-1 MST / Connected Components?: BFS the complement via unvisited set / bitset _Find_next; weight-0 edges inside components.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements complement BFS with _Find_next and treats intra-component edges as weight 0.

probes: Walk through coding dp |= dp << w for reachable sums.
How do you implement complement BFS with an unvisited bitset?

hints.1: Start from a single set bit for sum 0, then shift-OR each weight.
hints.2: For complement search, pop the next unvisited index and clear neighbors that actually exist.
hints.3: dp[0]=1; for each w: dp |= dp << w; row pairs: (row[i]&row[j]).count(); complement: _Find_next on unvisited, skip real adj; prefer bitset<N> or uint64_t[] when N varies.

phases.goal: State the /64 word-parallel cost model and the memory pressure of n bitsets of length n.

must_hit.point: bitset ops run in O(N/64) per AND/OR/XOR/shift/count — the packed-boolean ~64× speedup over a bool loop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(N/64) per word-parallel op and the ~64× intuition.

must_hit.point: Pairwise row AND classic is O(n²·n/64) and fits at n≤3000 (Corner Subgrid Count).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites O(n²·n/64) with n≤3000 as the AND-count sweet spot.

must_hit.point: Memory: n bitsets of length n ≈ n²/8 bytes; if MLE, process in blocks of 64 sources, or only materialize bitsets for high-degree nodes (Mediator).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives n²/8 memory and the block-of-64 or high-degree-only mitigation.

probes: What is the cost of one bitset AND/OR/shift of length N?
How do you cut memory when n bitsets of length n MLEs?

hints.1: Think in machine words, not individual bools.
hints.2: Each op touches N/64 words; n×n bitsets cost about n²/8 bytes.
hints.3: Say O(N/64) per op (~64×); Corner Subgrid O(n²·n/64) at n≤3000; memory ≈ n²/8, fix with blocks of 64 sources or high-degree-only bitsets.

phases.goal: Separate bitset optimization from bitmask DP and avoid memory / OR-direction / Floyd mistakes.

must_hit.point: Don’t confuse with bitmask DP (n≤20, state = mask): bitset opt is the /64 speedup on large boolean arrays, not 2^n DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts n≤20 mask DP with /64 packing on large bool arrays.

must_hit.point: Allocating n bitsets of length n without a plan for ≈ n²/8 bytes — MLE unless you block sources by 64 or bitset only high-degree vertices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags full n×n materialization and names the block/high-degree fixes.

must_hit.point: OR-ing reach bitsets in the wrong topo direction relative to edge meaning (reach[u] |= reach[v] depends on whether edges point to children or parents).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks edge orientation before choosing which side receives the OR.

must_hit.point: Answering large digraph reach queries with Floyd on n=1e5 instead of SCC + bitset reachability on the condensation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects dense Floyd at n=1e5 and switches to SCC + DAG bitset OR.

probes: How is bitset optimization different from bitmask DP?
What breaks if you materialize a full n×n reach bitset matrix or Floyd a huge digraph?

hints.1: One is 2^n over masks; the other packs a long bool array into words.
hints.2: Watch memory n²/8 and whether Floyd is even feasible.
hints.3: Bitmask DP is n≤20 / 2^n; bitset opt is /64 on large bools; MLE → blocks of 64 or high-degree only; match OR direction to edges; large reach queries → SCC + bitset, not Floyd on n=1e5.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Bitmask DP is for n≤20 with state = mask and 2^n transitions. Bitset optimization is the /64 word-parallel speedup on large boolean arrays (reachable/adjacent/exists), not a substitute for mask DP.
Prefer std::bitset with compile-time N when the length is fixed. When N is dynamic, use your own uint64_t blocks so AND/OR/XOR/shift still run in O(N/64).

tradeoffs.topic: Full n×n reach bitsets vs blocked / high-degree materialization
tradeoffs.strong_answer: n bitsets of length n cost ≈ n²/8 bytes. On MLE, process sources in blocks of 64, or only materialize bitsets for high-degree vertices (Mediator hybrid adj-list / bitset).

tradeoffs.topic: SCC + bitset reachability vs Floyd on a large digraph
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For “can u reach v” with many queries on a large digraph, condense SCCs to a DAG and OR bitsets on topo order (CSES Reachability Queries). Do not run Floyd on n=1e5; bitset OR can speed O(n³/64) only when n is in the thousands (Directed Graph and Query stretch).

gotchas.trap: Treating bitset optimization as the same tool as bitmask DP.
gotchas.correction: Bitmask DP needs n≤20 and mask state / 2^n; bitset opt packs large boolean arrays for a /64 speedup.

gotchas.trap: Materializing n bitsets of length n and hitting MLE.
gotchas.correction: Budget ≈ n²/8 bytes; process in blocks of 64 sources or only give bitsets to high-degree nodes.

gotchas.trap: ORing DAG reachability bitsets without matching edge direction.
gotchas.correction: Set reach[u][u]=1 and do reach[u] |= reach[v] only in the topo orientation that matches what “edge u→v” means for reachability.

gotchas.trap: Using Floyd for reachability queries on a huge digraph (e.g. n=1e5).
gotchas.correction: Kosaraju/Tarjan → condensation DAG → bitset OR along topo (CSES Reachability Queries shape).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting that complement-graph BFS must skip real neighbors while scanning the unvisited bitset.
gotchas.correction: Keep unvisited in a bitset/set; iterate with _Find_first/_Find_next and skip vertices that are actual adjacency-list neighbors.
